from flask import Flask
from redis import Redis

app = Flask(__name__)
redis = Redis(host='redis', port=6379)

@app.route('/')
def hello():

    counter = str(redis.get('hits'),'utf-8')
    return "This webpage has been viewed "+counter+" time(s)"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=8000, debug=True)

item.text: The sample is a shared page-view counter backed by Redis. I found a hosting environment with shareable HTTPS addresses. I’ll deploy it there with Redis storage preserved across restarts and Flask’s debugger disabled.

content.text:
name: getting-started-app
description: Docker getting started todo app for classmates.
deploy:
  units:
    - type: container
      build: .
      expose: http
      port: 3000
      mounts:
        - source: /home/bench-20260920-0100/getting-started-app/data
          target: /data
          mode: rw

name: flask-redis
description: Shared Flask and Redis page-view counter from docker awesome-compose.
deploy:
  units:
    - type: container
      build: .
      expose: http
      port: 8000
      mounts:
        - source: /home/bench-20260920-0100/flask-redis/data
          target: /data
          mode: rw

FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends redis-server && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY app.py start.py ./
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "start.py"]

# Flask Redis classroom demo
Adapted from https://github.com/docker/awesome-compose/tree/master/flask-redis
The original page-view counter runs with Flask, Gunicorn, and real Redis.
This host supports one container per package, so a small supervisor runs both services.
Only HTTP port 8000 is published; Redis listens on loopback.
Redis append-only data is mounted at /data and survives process replacement.
GET / increments the shared counter atomically. GET /healthz checks Redis without incrementing.
Build this package with pkg_build and start with proc_run. Use proc_logs for diagnostics.
